title: Length, Width & Projecting Loads
whatItIs: Loads that stick out at the front, rear or sides must be made visible. Longer projections need marker boards, an attendant or police notice. Signs can ban vehicles over a set width or length.

keyFacts.text: A vehicle MUST NOT be used or loaded in a way that endangers people in it or other road users.

keyFacts: Projecting more than 2 m at the front or rear: end and side projection markers are needed.
Over 3.05 m at the front or rear: 2 clear working days' notice to the police, an attendant and marker boards.

keyFacts.text: Vehicles with projecting loads MUST NOT be left on a road at night without lights.

visual.caption: Front and rear projections: what the regulations require

notes: Side projection over 305 mm: police notice, marker boards and extra lights in the dark.

onTheTest.question: Your load projects 2.5 metres beyond the front of your vehicle. What's required?
options: Only the end made clearly visible
onTheTest.why: A forward projection over 2 m needs an attendant and marker boards. Over 3.05 m, the police also need 2 clear working days' notice.

onTheTest.question: You see a red-ringed circular sign showing a width in metres and feet. What does it mean?
options: The road narrows to the width shown
No vehicles over the width shown
onTheTest.why: This regulatory sign means no vehicles over the maximum width shown. A similar sign shows a maximum length for vehicles or combinations.

traps: Front and rear differ: a forward projection over 2 m needs an attendant, a rearward one only over 3.05 m.
Police notice means 2 clear working days, not counting Sundays or bank holidays.
Overhang of 1 m or less: no marking requirements are specified.
